title: The Tarantula Nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud
caption: The Tarantula Nebula, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This view from ESO's VLT Survey Telescope shows the Tarantula Nebula, a gigantic star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a neighboring galaxy of the Milky Way. It lies in the direction of the constellation Dorado.

An astonishing number of massive stars are born in the Tarantula. Some of them might reach masses of up to 300 times that of the Sun, although that figure is a possibility rather than a firm measurement.

Star-forming regions like this are vast clouds of gas and dust. Dense pockets collapse under their own gravity to form new stars, and the most massive of these newborn stars pour out energy that makes the surrounding gas glow. In the Tarantula, that process has produced an unusually large crop of heavyweight stars.

understand.summary: This image comes from the OmegaCAM camera on ESO's VLT Survey Telescope, using visible and near-infrared filters plus one that isolates glowing hydrogen. The colors assigned to each filter are not published.
